questions.stem: Which next study best resolves whether the outside conduction result supports an intervention for {patientName}'s hand symptoms?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Symptoms
items.value: Intermittent numbness wakes the patient and affects the thumb, index and middle fingers. Grip is limited by the sensory symptoms.

items.label: Acquisition sheet
items.value: The hand skin temperature was 25 C. The report's abnormal conclusion used an isolated absolute median distal latency; no same-distance control-nerve comparison was recorded.

items.label: Competing record
items.value: An older cervical MRI described right foraminal narrowing. Current examination shows preserved proximal arm strength and no radiating neck-to-arm pain.

answerChoices.label: Temperature-controlled median and control-nerve conduction studies
answerChoices.rationale: The sensory map makes a distal median process plausible, but this isolated absolute measurement is confounded. A controlled comparative acquisition can establish whether focal slowing is real.

answerChoices.label: Needle EMG of cervical paraspinal and proximal arm muscles
answerChoices.rationale: The old foraminal image is a plausible competing explanation, but the current distribution does not supply proximal findings that outweigh the unresolved distal measurement.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The old foraminal image is a plausible competing explanation, but the current distribution does not supply proximal findings that outweigh the unresolved distal measurement.

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound of the median nerve and flexor tendons
answerChoices.rationale: Anatomic ultrasound can address a structural wrist question, but it does not determine whether this temperature-sensitive physiological result demonstrates focal conduction slowing.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Anatomic ultrasound can address a structural wrist question, but it does not determine whether this temperature-sensitive physiological result demonstrates focal conduction slowing.

questions.explanation: The symptoms and the acquisition must be interpreted separately. This record supports considering a distal median process but does not yet supply an adequately controlled physiological confirmation. The key corrects this particular confounder; it does not mean every cold-hand study is uninterpretable or that symptoms alone mandate surgery.

questions.stem: Which referral plan should lead treatment of {patientName}'s progressive hand motor loss?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Observed movement
items.value: With the palm flat, the thumb cannot abduct perpendicular to the palm against resistance. The thenar contour has flattened and buttoning has become harder.

items.label: Conduction and sampling
items.value: Median conduction is selectively slowed across the carpal segment relative to same-distance control nerves, with a reduced thenar motor response. Sampled proximal arm muscles retain normal voluntary recruitment.

items.label: Competing trends
items.value: A local corticosteroid injection substantially reduced the tingling, but thumb power has continued to fall. An older cervical MRI also describes right foraminal narrowing.

answerChoices.label: Hand-surgical assessment for carpal tunnel release
answerChoices.rationale: Selective distal conduction abnormality and progressive palmar-abduction weakness make the motor course consequential even though tingling improved.

answerChoices.label: Spine-surgical assessment for cervical root decompression
answerChoices.rationale: The cervical image is a real competing record, but it is less concordant with the selective distal physiology and thenar deficit than the hand-level findings.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The cervical image is a real competing record, but it is less concordant with the selective distal physiology and thenar deficit than the hand-level findings.

answerChoices.label: Hand-therapy review for continued conservative symptom care
answerChoices.rationale: Sensory improvement makes this tempting, but continued motor deterioration means symptom relief has not resolved the consequential deficit.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Sensory improvement makes this tempting, but continued motor deterioration means symptom relief has not resolved the consequential deficit.

questions.explanation: Palmar abduction is specified so the observed deficit is not confused with thumb extension. The current motor trajectory and focal physiology outweigh sensory improvement and an uncorrelated cervical image for this referral decision. This is an assessment for release, not a rule that an old MRI excludes coexisting root disease.

questions.stem: Which investigation should lead evaluation of {patientName}'s worsening hand function and walking difficulty?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Initial record
items.value: Right little/ring-finger tingling began after the operation. An outside study found mild focal slowing across the elbow, and protective positioning reduced that tingling.

items.label: Current hand findings
items.value: Fine finger movements are now slow in both hands, including thumb-index tasks; the patient drops small objects despite the sensory improvement.

items.label: Current walking examination
items.value: Tandem walking is unsteady. Both knee reflexes are brisk with sustained ankle clonus; lower-limb power had previously been recorded as normal.

answerChoices.label: MRI of the cervical spine
answerChoices.rationale: Bilateral hand dysfunction plus upper motor neuron and gait findings cannot be explained by the focal elbow result; cervical cord assessment addresses the broader pattern.

answerChoices.label: MRI of the right brachial plexus
answerChoices.rationale: A postoperative arm problem can prompt plexus imaging, but a unilateral plexus lesion does not account for the bilateral hand and leg findings.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A postoperative arm problem can prompt plexus imaging, but a unilateral plexus lesion does not account for the bilateral hand and leg findings.

answerChoices.label: MRI of the right elbow
answerChoices.rationale: The local study and initial paresthesia make this plausible, but a local elbow image will not resolve the new bilateral and lower-limb pattern.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The local study and initial paresthesia make this plausible, but a local elbow image will not resolve the new bilateral and lower-limb pattern.

questions.explanation: The initial focal finding need not be false to be insufficient. The resident must localize the newly broader examination before choosing imaging: hand dysfunction with gait and upper motor neuron findings raises a cervical cord concern. No diagnosis or operative technique is established before imaging.

questions.stem: Which management plan best fits {patientName}'s current elbow and hand findings?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Clinical trend
items.value: Protective elbow positioning has reduced right little/ring-finger tingling. Right finger spreading is progressively weaker and the first dorsal interosseous contour is flattening.

items.label: Paired examination and studies
items.value: Right elbow conduction is focally slowed with reduced intrinsic motor response and spontaneous activity in the first dorsal interosseous. Left hand strength, sensation and conduction remain normal.

items.label: Bilateral ultrasound
items.value: The ulnar nerve moves anterior to the medial epicondyle during flexion on each side. The left arm has no symptoms.

answerChoices.label: Refer for right cubital-tunnel surgical assessment
answerChoices.rationale: The right motor trajectory and concordant physiology justify escalation despite sensory improvement; bilateral mobility does not establish bilateral symptomatic disease.

answerChoices.label: Continue protective elbow care with clinical follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: This fits the sensory improvement but underweights progressive objective right motor loss and muscle wasting.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This fits the sensory improvement but underweights progressive objective right motor loss and muscle wasting.

answerChoices.label: Refer for bilateral cubital-tunnel surgical assessment
answerChoices.rationale: The ultrasound shows mobility on both sides, but the left side has no clinical or physiological neuropathy to justify the same escalation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The ultrasound shows mobility on both sides, but the left side has no clinical or physiological neuropathy to justify the same escalation.

questions.explanation: The current decision concerns progressive right motor dysfunction, not obtaining a dynamic image. Less tingling does not reverse the recorded weakness. The asymptomatic left arm demonstrates why a mobility finding must be clinically correlated; the draft does not choose decompression versus transposition or declare mobility harmless in every patient.

questions.stem: Which current management plan best fits {patientName}'s postoperative shoulder trajectory?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Initial postoperative findings
items.value: After an outside posterior-triangle lymph-node excision, the right shoulder rested lower, shrug was weak and overhead reach was limited. Initial trapezius sampling showed greatly reduced voluntary recruitment.

items.label: Serial function
items.value: With supervised rehabilitation, overhead reach and resisted shrug have improved on successive examinations. The scapular outline remains asymmetric.

items.label: Repeat sampling
items.value: The same trapezius regions now show new voluntary motor units with greater recruitment than on the baseline study.

answerChoices.label: Continue supervised shoulder rehabilitation and reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: Actual functional recovery and returning recruitment support ongoing conservative care despite persistent visible asymmetry.

answerChoices.label: Refer for spinal-accessory nerve exploration
answerChoices.rationale: The operation and initial deficit make this a credible pathway, but current recovery and new recruitment do not support escalation on appearance alone.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The operation and initial deficit make this a credible pathway, but current recovery and new recruitment do not support escalation on appearance alone.

answerChoices.label: Refer for scapular tendon-transfer reconstruction
answerChoices.rationale: A fixed persistent deficit may eventually create a reconstruction question, but this record documents improving neural and functional performance.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A fixed persistent deficit may eventually create a reconstruction question, but this record documents improving neural and functional performance.

questions.explanation: The operation and initial movement localize the problem, but they do not establish transection or a reconstruction deadline. Returning voluntary recruitment together with improving function changes the next plan. The evidence supports a recovery principle; Melissa must confirm this exact pathway, and no fixed repair window is authored.

questions.stem: Which initial outside-hospital plan best fit {patientName}'s knee presentation at this stage?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Initial outside examination
items.value: The right native knee was swollen and warm, with a palpable effusion and marked pain throughout passive motion. Fever and an elevated CRP were recorded.

items.label: Systemic assessment
items.value: Blood pressure, mentation and peripheral perfusion remained normal; no organ dysfunction was documented.

items.label: Treatment record
items.value: Blood cultures had been collected. The medication record showed analgesia but no antimicrobial administration.

answerChoices.label: Aspirate the knee, then start empiric antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: The joint findings warrant urgent microbiologic sampling. In this stable recorded stage, sampling before antibiotics avoids unnecessary loss of diagnostic yield.

answerChoices.label: Start empiric antibiotics, then aspirate the knee
answerChoices.rationale: The record supplies a stable opportunity for joint sampling; giving antibiotics first can compromise microbiologic confirmation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The record supplies a stable opportunity for joint sampling; giving antibiotics first can compromise microbiologic confirmation.

answerChoices.label: Obtain knee MRI, then aspirate the knee
answerChoices.rationale: The clinically evident effusion can be sampled without first resolving a structural MRI question. MRI-first postpones the key microbiologic step.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The clinically evident effusion can be sampled without first resolving a structural MRI question. MRI-first postpones the key microbiologic step.

questions.explanation: Concerning native-joint findings require synovial microbiology. The stable systemic observations permit joint sampling before empiric antibiotics. The sequence changes when sepsis makes treatment delay unsafe.

questions.stem: Which ultrasound-guided aspiration plan best addresses the unresolved cause of {patientName}'s painful native knee?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Fluid report
items.value: The submitted fluid contained monosodium urate crystals and neutrophils; no organisms were seen on Gram stain, and culture was pending.

items.label: Procedure images
items.value: The saved needle tip ends in a fluid pocket between the skin and patella. A separate suprapatellar joint effusion is visible.

items.label: Current examination
items.value: Fever and marked pain through passive knee motion persist. Redness and the superficial pocket cover the anterior patella; skin over the lateral suprapatellar recess is intact.

answerChoices.label: Lateral suprapatellar entry into the joint
answerChoices.rationale: The first sample does not establish the contents of the joint. This route obtains joint fluid while avoiding the inflamed superficial anterior pocket.

answerChoices.label: Anterior entry through the pocket into the joint
answerChoices.rationale: This would reach the relevant deeper compartment but traverse the overlying inflamed collection, creating an avoidable contamination or inoculation concern.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This would reach the relevant deeper compartment but traverse the overlying inflamed collection, creating an avoidable contamination or inoculation concern.

answerChoices.label: Anterior entry into the prepatellar pocket
answerChoices.rationale: The pocket may need evaluation in its own right, but its fluid will still not represent the separate joint effusion responsible for the unresolved intra-articular concern.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The pocket may need evaluation in its own right, but its fluid will still not represent the separate joint effusion responsible for the unresolved intra-articular concern.

questions.explanation: A label does not replace specimen provenance. The images show what was sampled; crystals and a negative stain in that fluid do not settle the separate joint question. The new sample must reach the joint through an appropriate route. This sampling decision does not suspend needed systemic treatment or establish that every superficial collection communicates with the joint.

questions.stem: Which requested analysis should receive priority for {patientName}'s limited repeat knee aspirate?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: New result
items.value: The synovial bacterial PCR detected S. aureus; the original culture had not produced an isolate.

items.label: Repeat aspiration
items.value: The laboratory received a small amount of newly aspirated fluid and reported that it could not perform every requested test.

items.label: Requested tests
items.value: Bacterial culture, leukocyte count and crystal examination were all requested.

answerChoices.label: Bacterial culture of the new aspirate
answerChoices.rationale: Bacterial identification remains the priority when volume is limited. A PCR detection has not provided a viable isolate for standard susceptibility testing.

answerChoices.label: Leukocyte count of the new aspirate
answerChoices.rationale: A numerical inflammatory count cannot substitute for bacterial identification in this unresolved culture workup.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A numerical inflammatory count cannot substitute for bacterial identification in this unresolved culture workup.

answerChoices.label: Crystal microscopy of the new aspirate
answerChoices.rationale: Crystals could coexist with infection and should not displace bacterial identification when fluid is scarce.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Crystals could coexist with infection and should not displace bacterial identification when fluid is scarce.

questions.explanation: Use scarce synovial material to preserve bacterial identification first. The positive molecular result does not create a cultured isolate, and an inflammatory count or crystal result cannot replace it.

questions.stem: Which next treatment step best fit {patientName}'s knee at this recorded reassessment?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Earlier care
items.value: The hospital performed an arthroscopic washout of an infected native knee and started antibiotics active against the recovered organism.

items.label: Interval findings
items.value: Purulent drainage and a reaccumulating effusion continued; passive motion became more painful, and CRP rose on serial measurements.

items.label: Treatment verification
items.value: The susceptibility report and medication record remained concordant, with no missed antimicrobial doses.

answerChoices.label: Repeat arthroscopic knee debridement
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent purulence, deteriorating function and rising inflammatory markers support failed source control despite an active antimicrobial regimen.

answerChoices.label: Change to broader intravenous antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: The available susceptibility and administration record do not identify inadequate antimicrobial activity; the local purulent course requires renewed source-control attention.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The available susceptibility and administration record do not identify inadequate antimicrobial activity; the local purulent course requires renewed source-control attention.

answerChoices.label: Continue the current intravenous antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: Passive continuation overlooks combined evidence of local treatment failure.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Passive continuation overlooks combined evidence of local treatment failure.

questions.explanation: An active antibiotic does not establish adequate source control. The combined local deterioration and inflammatory trend support repeat orthopedic debridement assessment, without claiming that any single CRP value mandates surgery.

questions.stem: Which immediate evaluation should lead the outside team's response to {patientName}'s worsening postoperative leg findings?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Block and motor course
items.value: The regional block had resolved with initially documented ankle movement. Later examinations showed progressively weaker ankle dorsiflexion and toe movement.

items.label: Local findings
items.value: Deep calf pain rose despite analgesia. The calf became swollen and firm, and passive toe movement markedly increased pain.

items.label: Perfusion
items.value: The foot remained warm with palpable pedal pulses.

answerChoices.label: Immediate surgical assessment of calf compartments
answerChoices.rationale: The progressive deep pain, stretch pain, firmness and evolving motor deficit require bedside assessment for treatable local pressure despite preserved pulses.

answerChoices.label: Immediate venous assessment with leg duplex ultrasound
answerChoices.rationale: Postoperative swelling makes venous thrombosis a credible concern, but duplex does not resolve the combined stretch pain, firmness and worsening motor deficit that need direct compartment assessment.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Postoperative swelling makes venous thrombosis a credible concern, but duplex does not resolve the combined stretch pain, firmness and worsening motor deficit that need direct compartment assessment.

answerChoices.label: Immediate peripheral-nerve assessment with electrodiagnosis
answerChoices.rationale: Progressive weakness deserves specialist attention, but physiology is not the first way to exclude a surgically treatable local pressure problem in this painful swollen limb.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Progressive weakness deserves specialist attention, but physiology is not the first way to exclude a surgically treatable local pressure problem in this painful swollen limb.

questions.explanation: The deficit appeared after block resolution and is progressing with local pain and swelling. Palpable pulses assess arterial flow but do not exclude a compartment pressure problem. Surgical bedside assessment must address reversible compression; pressure measurement may assist when indicated. The draft neither diagnoses a specific mechanism from timing nor substitutes consultation for examining the limb.

questions.stem: Which next spine study best fit {patientName}'s initial outside evaluation?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Symptoms
items.value: Focal lumbar pain persisted at rest and repeatedly woke the patient from sleep.

items.label: Outside evaluation
items.value: The patient was afebrile, with unchanged leg strength and sensation. CRP remained above the laboratory reference range.

items.label: Existing imaging
items.value: Lumbar radiographs showed osteophytes and disc-space narrowing without an acute fracture; no cross-sectional spine imaging had been performed.

answerChoices.label: Contrast-enhanced lumbar spine MRI
answerChoices.rationale: The infection history and inflammatory course remain concerning despite absent fever and degenerative radiographs. MRI evaluates early vertebral/disc and adjacent soft-tissue infection.

answerChoices.label: Noncontrast lumbar spine CT
answerChoices.rationale: CT is useful for bony detail but is not the preferred next assessment of this suspected disc/soft-tissue process when MRI is feasible.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: CT is useful for bony detail but is not the preferred next assessment of this suspected disc/soft-tissue process when MRI is feasible.

answerChoices.label: Technetium lumbar bone scan
answerChoices.rationale: A bone scan is not preferred when MRI can assess the vertebral and adjacent soft-tissue process.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A bone scan is not preferred when MRI can assess the vertebral and adjacent soft-tissue process.

questions.explanation: Afebrile status and degenerative films do not adequately explain persistent focal pain with continuing inflammatory evidence. MRI addresses the vertebral/disc and adjacent soft-tissue question.

questions.stem: Which initial sampling and treatment sequence best fits {patientName}'s current spinal record? In these plans, treatment after sampling means after specimen acquisition, not after final culture results.

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: MRI observations
items.value: Opposing lumbar endplate marrow abnormalities and intervening disc enhancement accompany adjacent paraspinal inflammation. There is no epidural collection, neural compression or destructive deformity.

items.label: Microbiology and medication record
items.value: Blood cultures collected at the initial evaluation have finalized without growth. No antimicrobial dose has been administered since collection.

items.label: Current clinical state
items.value: Blood pressure and perfusion are normal; the patient is alert. Leg power, sensation and bladder/bowel function remain unchanged. No spinal procedure has yet been performed.

answerChoices.label: Image-guided disc/endplate sampling before starting empiric antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: Stable physiology and neurology allow initial microbiologic/histologic tissue acquisition. Without an operative indication, image-guided sampling is the less invasive initial diagnostic route.

answerChoices.label: Empiric antibiotics before obtaining image-guided disc/endplate samples
answerChoices.rationale: The acquisition route is reasonable, but in this untreated stable record it gives up the opportunity to obtain tissue before antimicrobial exposure.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The acquisition route is reasonable, but in this untreated stable record it gives up the opportunity to obtain tissue before antimicrobial exposure.

answerChoices.label: Open operative disc/endplate sampling before starting empiric antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: Sampling before treatment fits the stated stable phase, but no compressive or mechanical finding supplies an initial operative reason over image-guided acquisition.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Sampling before treatment fits the stated stable phase, but no compressive or mechanical finding supplies an initial operative reason over image-guided acquisition.

answerChoices.label: Empiric antibiotics before obtaining open operative disc/endplate samples
answerChoices.rationale: This combines treatment-first exposure with an open route not justified by the current stability and imaging findings.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This combines treatment-first exposure with an open route not justified by the current stability and imaging findings.

questions.explanation: The decision boundary is specimen acquisition. The untreated, stable patient with negative blood cultures needs etiologic tissue information, and the record gives no initial decompression or stabilization indication. Empiric treatment can begin after specimens are obtained; this question does not require waiting for final cultures or select a drug regimen.

questions.stem: Which treatment response plan best fits {patientName}'s current spinal record?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Established disease
items.value: The outside team treated culture-confirmed vertebral infection with susceptibility-concordant antibiotics.

items.label: Clinical course
items.value: The patient was afebrile; pain and walking tolerance improved. Leg strength and bladder/bowel function were unchanged. CRP fell toward the reference range.

items.label: Repeat MRI
items.value: The report described more prominent endplate/disc abnormalities but no new epidural collection, neural compression or deformity.

answerChoices.label: Continue the planned pathogen-directed treatment
answerChoices.rationale: Clinical/inflammatory improvement can coexist with evolving bony MRI abnormalities; the scan does not establish failure here.

answerChoices.label: Replace treatment with broader empiric antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: The scan does not establish resistance or inadequate treatment during documented clinical response.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The scan does not establish resistance or inadequate treatment during documented clinical response.

answerChoices.label: Proceed to operative spinal debridement
answerChoices.rationale: No compression, deformity or clinical failure is documented to supply a surgical indication.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: No compression, deformity or clinical failure is documented to supply a surgical indication.

questions.explanation: The response supports continuing planned treatment. MRI normalization need not coincide with clinical improvement. New neural or mechanical problems would require a different assessment; no treatment-stop rule is asserted.

questions.stem: While continuing bloodstream-infection treatment, which next diagnostic plan best addresses {patientName}'s two spinal sites?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Microbiology and shared treatment
items.value: Separate pre-treatment blood-culture sets grew methicillin-susceptible S. aureus. Susceptibility-directed therapy is being administered and continues under every proposed plan.

items.label: Lumbar site
items.value: At L3-L4, MRI shows opposing endplate abnormalities, intervening disc enhancement and adjacent soft-tissue inflammation corresponding to the focal pain.

items.label: Separate thoracic site
items.value: At T8, there is a discrete destructive vertebral/pedicle lesion with a solid adjacent mass; the neighboring discs retain their usual signal. No tissue has been sampled from either site.

items.label: Current state
items.value: The patient is hemodynamically stable without new weakness or bladder/bowel dysfunction.

answerChoices.label: Image-guided T8 lesion biopsy for culture and histology
answerChoices.rationale: The bloodstream isolate fits the lumbar disc/endplate pattern, but it does not automatically explain a structurally different thoracic lesion. Tissue at the unresolved site can address infection and mimickers.

answerChoices.label: Image-guided L3-L4 biopsy for culture and histology
answerChoices.rationale: This could resample a site already concordant with the bloodstream evidence while leaving the distinct thoracic process unresolved.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This could resample a site already concordant with the bloodstream evidence while leaving the distinct thoracic process unresolved.

answerChoices.label: Treatment of both sites with follow-up spinal imaging
answerChoices.rationale: This correctly preserves active bacteremia treatment but assumes the separate lesion shares the lumbar cause without resolving its different structural pattern.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This correctly preserves active bacteremia treatment but assumes the separate lesion shares the lumbar cause without resolving its different structural pattern.

questions.explanation: A convincing blood isolate can remove the need for a routine diagnostic biopsy of a matching spinal infection. That inference is site specific. A distinct lesion with a different structural pattern can merit its own culture and histology while treatment of proven bacteremia continues. Disc preservation does not prove a tumor or exclude infection; it contributes to unresolved concordance.

questions.stem: Alongside urgent specialist assessment, which first investigation best addresses {patientName}'s new neurological findings during treatment of lumbar infection?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Earlier documented state
items.value: The patient was walking and emptying the bladder normally when treatment for the lumbar infection began.

items.label: Treatment trajectory
items.value: Susceptibility-directed antibiotics have reduced fever and CRP. The last imaging was obtained before the new neurological findings.

items.label: New examination
items.value: Both legs have become progressively weaker. Ankle movement and perineal sensation are reduced, and the patient newly cannot empty the bladder.

answerChoices.label: Urgent contrast MRI of the lumbar spine
answerChoices.rationale: The bilateral motor, perineal and bladder findings localize the new concern to spinal neural structures. MRI can assess the canal and epidural tissues despite systemic improvement.

answerChoices.label: Urgent contrast CT of the lumbar spine
answerChoices.rationale: CT provides valuable bony information and can be used when MRI cannot be obtained, but MRI is preferred here for the new neural and epidural question.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: CT provides valuable bony information and can be used when MRI cannot be obtained, but MRI is preferred here for the new neural and epidural question.

answerChoices.label: Urgent nerve conduction and lower-limb EMG
answerChoices.rationale: Physiology may clarify a peripheral deficit, but it is not the first investigation of this bilateral motor, perineal and bladder pattern during spinal infection.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Physiology may clarify a peripheral deficit, but it is not the first investigation of this bilateral motor, perineal and bladder pattern during spinal infection.

questions.explanation: The learner has not been given a new MRI diagnosis. The examination must first be localized and then matched to an investigation suited to the canal and epidural tissues. Falling fever and CRP do not settle a new neural problem. Urgent specialist assessment occurs in parallel; no imaging delay or predetermined decompressive operation is endorsed.

questions.stem: Which study best clarifies {patientName}'s foot-drop localization before a lumbar intervention is considered?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Outside context
items.value: Right foot drop appeared after a prolonged nonorthopedic operation. A preoperative lumbar MRI already showed right foraminal narrowing.

items.label: Current examination
items.value: Dorsiflexion and eversion are weak; inversion and hip abduction remain strong. Sensory loss affects the dorsal foot.

items.label: Clinical course
items.value: The deficit persists; the MRI predates it and no electrodiagnostic localization is available.

answerChoices.label: Fibular nerve conduction and needle EMG
answerChoices.rationale: The motor map favors a fibular-territory process over one affecting additional root muscles. EDX can localize the current deficit rather than assume an older MRI finding caused it.

answerChoices.label: Repeat lumbar MRI with foraminal assessment
answerChoices.rationale: The pre-deficit narrowing does not establish the cause of this nerve-territory pattern. Localization is needed before a lumbar intervention.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The pre-deficit narrowing does not establish the cause of this nerve-territory pattern. Localization is needed before a lumbar intervention.

answerChoices.label: Tibial nerve conduction and needle EMG
answerChoices.rationale: An isolated tibial-focused assessment does not interrogate the main weak dorsiflexion/eversion territory.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: An isolated tibial-focused assessment does not interrogate the main weak dorsiflexion/eversion territory.

questions.explanation: Fit the current motor map before assigning causation to an image. Preserved nonfibular functions and an MRI predating the deficit favor fibular-directed EDX. Postoperative timing alone does not prove an anesthetic or positioning cause.

reviewRecords.title: Median neuropathy: prior study scope
clarityIssues: The recurring update, "review the next dated outside-clinic record", supplies neither a date nor a clinical change. It is navigation text rather than decision information.

cues.phrase: placing the wrist in flexion reproduces it
cues.why: The symptomatic wrist and the neutral wrist splint both repeat the anatomical word present in only one option. This reinforces a simple location match.

cues.phrase: Ulnar conduction across the elbow
cues.why: This option repeats the explicitly normal outside study verbatim; the novelty advantage favors the unperformed study.

fairness: Median wrist testing is the defensible best target among these options; no confident clinical error is identified in the explanation.
Deleting the outside study still leaves the same classic median-wrist answer. Localizing the pattern and naming that same segment for testing do not create two consequential decisions.
First node is self-contained; its feedback does not disclose the later treatment answer.
suggestions: Retain the high-yield localization objective, but make actual study adequacy change whether or where further investigation is needed.
Compare credible localization/next-test plans that cannot be discarded simply because they repeat a normal study; retain necessary nerve and segment details.
Remove the generic update or replace it with a meaningful chronology marker.

reviewRecords.title: Median neuropathy: progressive motor deficit
clarityIssues: "The thumb cannot lift away from the palm against resistance" does not clearly distinguish palmar abduction from thumb extension or radial abduction. Specify the tested motion.

cues.phrase: The wrist splint and a prior carpal-tunnel corticosteroid injection gave only temporary relief
cues.why: Both nonsurgical options repeat treatments the exhibit says have failed.

cues.phrase: Another carpal-tunnel corticosteroid injection / Another trial of neutral wrist splinting
cues.why: Both distractors advertise repetition with "Another"; the key is the only escalation/new action.

fairness: Concordant wrist localization, worsening motor function and thenar wasting support hand-surgical assessment. No competing option is equally persuasive as written.
The new study supplies the localization, leaving a single escalation decision against weak repeat-treatment alternatives.
The follow-up is coherent and independently supplies the study, deterioration and treatment history; prior feedback does not give away release.
suggestions: Describe palmar thumb abduction unambiguously.
Use a credible decision about treatment escalation with a patient-specific competing consideration, or seek explicit acceptance as an easy motor-loss safety item.
Do not weaken or remove motor-loss findings merely to manufacture difficulty.

reviewRecords.title: Ulnar neuropathy: focal electrodiagnostic assessment
clarityIssues: "Needle examination found abnormalities" is nonspecific; if these findings are meant to resolve competing localizations, describe the relevant observed pattern.

cues.phrase: Repeat averaged ulnar studies over the same span
cues.why: The option explicitly repeats the method already reported normal; only the short-segment option changes the relevant acquisition.

cues.phrase: Little/ring-finger tingling / ulnar intrinsic muscles / Median studies across the wrist segment
cues.why: The exhibit already names an ulnar process, making the lone median option a weak out-of-territory distractor.

fairness: Short-segment assessment is a plausible way to resolve a suspected focal elbow lesion despite a normal long-segment average; no numerical diagnostic claim is independently verified here.
The symptoms, needle interpretation and focal provocation already establish the intended territory. The item mainly recalls a technical acquisition refinement.
The first node stands alone and its explanation does not disclose the later ultrasound answer.

The exact long-segment versus short-segment technique is lower-yield for general-surgery boards than recognizing and localizing postoperative ulnar dysfunction; highYield=false refers to this scored objective.
suggestions: Refocus on a practical general-surgery decision changed by discordant localization evidence, or retain the acquisition detail only with an explicit supporting educational purpose.
Replace the median-wrist foil and the knowingly unchanged repeat with credible competing assessments.
Use observations that make the actual protocol interpretation consequential rather than just naming the abnormal nerve.

reviewRecords.title: Ulnar symptoms: dynamic elbow imaging

cues.phrase: a palpable snap occur as the elbow moves from extension into flexion
cues.why: The only option that contains the same motion is "Dynamic elbow ultrasound during flexion and extension"; no nerve knowledge is needed for the match.

cues.phrase: it contains no flexion/extension acquisition
cues.why: This names the missing acquisition that is the answer.

cues.phrase: Repeat resting elbow ultrasound in extension / Static elbow MRI with the arm extended
cues.why: Both competitors are explicitly static while the presentation repeatedly emphasizes motion.

fairness: Dynamic ultrasound is a defensible study for the unresolved snapping phenomenon; the item appropriately avoids assuming nerve movement proves a specific operation.
The earlier node establishes localization; this update restates it. A new structural objective exists, but the motion acquisition is supplied rather than inferred.

The follow-up is coherent and supplies its own localization and prior imaging. The exact dynamic imaging choice is a supporting specialty detail rather than a leading general-surgery testing objective.
suggestions: Remove the named-missing-acquisition sentence while preserving what the earlier scan actually assessed.
If retaining this objective, compare credible studies/plans without contrasting a single dynamic label against two explicitly static labels.
Add a real interpretive consequence or classify the item as basic after independent acceptance; do not call word matching two-step reasoning.

reviewRecords.title: Postoperative shoulder deficit: trapezius assessment

cues.phrase: The medial scapular border does not lift during forward pushing
cues.why: This negative directly disposes of the serratus competitor instead of leaving a close localization problem.

cues.phrase: Repeat needle examination of deltoid
cues.why: The remaining distractor repeats a specifically normal sample. The key is the only unexcluded target.

fairness: The posterior-triangle operation, shoulder droop and weak shrug support trapezius/accessory-territory assessment. No confident factual error is identified.
The outside normal samples can be deleted without changing the answer. Recognizing the muscle and ordering its needle examination are one localization operation, not two consequential steps.
This is a standalone case; it does not rely on the separate serratus case. Accessory nerve injury after neck surgery is high-yield.
suggestions: Keep the postoperative anatomy objective but introduce a credible competing localization or an assessment limitation that changes the next action.
Use plausible unsampled targets rather than an explicitly normal repeat as a disposable foil.
Retain necessary examination findings; remove only those serving solely as option-by-option exclusion.

reviewRecords.title: Postoperative scapular deficit: serratus assessment

cues.phrase: normal trapezius and deltoid needle samples
cues.why: These are precisely the two distractor targets.

cues.phrase: Repeat needle examination of trapezius / Repeat needle examination of deltoid
cues.why: Both wrong choices announce repeating normal work; the only new target can be selected without knowing which muscle controls forward pushing.

fairness: The forward-push winging pattern with preserved shrug supports serratus assessment. The explanation appropriately avoids claiming a recovery interval or operative indication.
The classic examination alone selects serratus; the outside test does not earn a second inference.
The case stands alone and is anatomically coherent. Long thoracic injury in the axillary operative setting is high-yield.
suggestions: Replace the two overt repeat-normal distractors with clinically credible alternatives at the same decision stage.
Make examination/test discordance alter a real care decision instead of testing an unexamined-muscle matching rule.
Preserve the distinction between localization and establishing injury mechanism or transection.

reviewRecords.title: Native knee infection: aspiration and antibiotic sequence
fairness: The painful effused native joint and inflammatory findings require infectious evaluation; normal perfusion, mentation and absence of organ dysfunction support sampling before empiric treatment in this presented stage.

The antibiotic-first option represents a real sequencing error, and MRI-first adds an unnecessary step before sampling an evident effusion. One defensible best answer is present without an invented laboratory threshold.
The retrospective task is complete and self-contained. The explanation does not disclose the later crystal/Gram-stain interpretation.
suggestions: Preserve the distinction between this stable stage and sepsis or circumstances in which obtaining a specimen would dangerously delay treatment.
Editorial PASS is not clinical approval or a fresh source verification; retain needs_clinician_review.

reviewRecords.title: Native knee infection: crystals and negative Gram stain

cues.phrase: Replace antimicrobials with oral colchicine / Replace antimicrobials with intra-articular steroid
cues.why: Both alternatives abandon the same treatment while one option preserves it; the steroid alternative is especially weak with unresolved infection and persistent fever.

fairness: Crystals and a negative Gram stain do not exclude concomitant infection. Continuing empiric antimicrobials while cultures and orthopedic reassessment continue is defensible.

The aspiration results introduce a real misconception, but the unchanged severe febrile course and two replacement alternatives reduce this to the familiar single rule that crystals do not exclude infection.
The follow-up is coherent and independently states the aspirate, pending cultures, ongoing symptoms and treatment. The preceding explanation does not supply the crystal rule.
suggestions: Retain this high-yield misconception but make the new data change a consequential diagnostic or source-control decision.
Use a credible competing interim plan; avoid making the alternatives two obvious ways to abandon unresolved infection treatment.
If retained as a safety recognition item, obtain explicit basic-item acceptance and label its predicted difficulty honestly.

reviewRecords.title: Culture-negative treated knee: molecular testing
clarityIssues: "Repeat Gram stain" and "Repeat crystal microscopy" presuppose prior examinations whose results are not supplied in this case. It is unclear what has already been learned or why repetition is offered.

cues.phrase: Bacterial PCR on synovial fluid
cues.why: This is the only new test; both other labels begin "Repeat". The novelty cue can bypass interpretation of antibiotic exposure.

fairness: Antibiotic exposure before sampling limits the exclusionary value of a negative culture; molecular testing is a plausible additional investigation for persistent suspected infection.

No confident clinical inaccuracy is asserted, but comparative yield and the intended assay are not independently verified offline. The test should not be taught as universally sensitive or a replacement for culture/source-control assessment.

The initial node is self-contained apart from the unspecified prior tests. Molecular testing in culture-negative native-joint infection is a narrower supporting topic than the core sampling/source-control principles.
suggestions: State relevant prior stain/crystal findings if repeat testing remains a competitor, or remove the unsupported repetition premise.
Compare genuinely plausible laboratory investigations without making PCR the only novel option.
Keep assay limitations in feedback and have a clinician confirm the exact ranking; prioritize the broader sampling principle if this lane must cover only the most commonly tested concepts.

reviewRecords.title: Limited knee aspirate: microbiology priority
fairness: The positive molecular result establishes an organism signal but does not supply a cultured isolate. Allocating scarce new fluid to culture requires recognizing that unresolved purpose and choosing among legitimate competing analyses.
The laboratory explicitly cannot perform all requested tests; the constraint is necessary rather than an arbitrary permission cue. The culture option does not require an invented minimum volume.

The follow-up coherently returns the earlier molecular result and independently supplies the result, lack of an isolate and limited specimen. Previous feedback supports PCR use but does not answer the allocation task.
This is high-yield at the level of preserving microbiologic identification/susceptibility opportunities, not memorizing a specialist volume cutoff.
suggestions: Consider mentioning the remaining susceptibility question in post-answer feedback to make the value of recovering an isolate concrete.
Keep the PCR result distinct from culture recovery and clinical approval; retain needs_clinician_review.

reviewRecords.title: Persistent knee infection despite active antibiotics
fairness: Persistent purulence, recurrent effusion, worsening passive-motion pain and rising inflammatory markers support failed source control despite a susceptibility-concordant administered regimen.

The learner must distinguish antimicrobial failure from inadequate drainage and select renewed debridement. Broader therapy and continuation represent plausible competing errors; the key is not selected by a single isolated CRP value.
The first node is self-contained. The later postoperative deficit is a separate complication after the repeat procedure rather than a contradiction of this node.
The description supports repeat operative source control; the precise arthroscopic versus open approach remains a clinician judgment and should not be generalized beyond this case.
suggestions: Retain the combined local trajectory and treatment verification rather than replacing them with the diagnosis label "failed source control".
Keep actual operative technique subject to clinical review; editorial PASS is not technique endorsement for every infected knee.

reviewRecords.title: Progressive postoperative weakness despite early normal EDX
clarityIssues: The task asks for an "evaluation plan", but the key names consultation without indicating whether immediate assessment for reversible postoperative compression is occurring. Normal distal perfusion does not resolve that question.

cues.phrase: Urgent neurology or peripheral-nerve consultation
cues.why: This is the only urgent action for an explicitly progressively worsening motor deficit.

cues.phrase: Scheduled repeat electrodiagnosis with later clinic review / Supervised rehabilitation with routine clinic review
cues.why: Both distractors advertise delay or routine follow-up; they do not create a close decision.

fairness: Escalating progressive objective weakness despite an early normal study is appropriate. The normal EDX does not safely justify routine follow-up.

The question does not support a specific operative/anesthetic cause. Urgent consultation is defensible, but the explanation should not imply that it substitutes for immediate bedside assessment of treatable compression; the absent findings do not justify diagnosing such a complication here.
The progression itself selects urgency even if the EDX row is deleted, so the normal-study issue adds a teaching point rather than a second consequential step.
The later node coherently follows another knee procedure and restates the block resolution and neurological course; it can stand alone.
suggestions: Clarify the immediate evaluation stage and relevant pain, swelling or local compression findings if these determine which urgent pathway is best.
Compare credible urgent evaluation plans, or request explicit acceptance of an easy safety-recognition exception.
Preserve progression and block-resolution observations; do not obscure urgency to create difficulty.

reviewRecords.title: Concerning back pain despite degenerative radiographs
fairness: Persistent focal rest/night pain with elevated CRP warrants investigation beyond a degenerative radiograph interpretation; MRI is the best of the listed studies for disc, vertebral and adjacent soft-tissue pathology.

The learner must resist anchoring on degenerative films and choose the modality suited to the remaining concern. CT and scintigraphy are genuine imaging alternatives without a conspicuous wording shortcut.
Absence of fever does not negate the concern, and the explanation does not claim these nonspecific findings prove infection.
The first node is self-contained and does not disclose the later biopsy/treatment sequence. No confident clinical inaccuracy is identified within the reviewed presentation and explanation.
suggestions: Keep the explanation framed as a reason to investigate, not a confirmed infectious diagnosis.
Do not add an infection history unless it is actually part of the visible case; retain needs_clinician_review.

reviewRecords.title: Stable culture-negative spinal infection: tissue acquisition
clarityIssues: Blood cultures "collected before antibiotics" does not say whether antibiotics have since been started. That matters to a task explicitly comparing pretreatment sampling sequences.
"then select antibiotics" leaves unclear whether treatment begins after obtaining the samples or only after their final results. The task should identify the intended decision boundary.

cues.phrase: spine specialists planned nonsurgical treatment
cues.why: This preannounces the nonsurgical route and directly weakens "Obtain open operative disc/endplate samples". The actual stability and compression findings should do that work.

fairness: With stable neurological/hemodynamic status, no identified organism and no operative indication, initial image-guided microbiologic/histologic sampling is defensible.
The sampling-before-empiric-treatment objective has two real elements, but the present antibiotic exposure and timing language prevent a fully precise single-best sequence.
The imaging result follows the previous MRI question coherently and can stand alone; the earlier explanation does not reveal the biopsy route.
suggestions: State whether any antimicrobials have been administered since blood collection.
Make option sequencing explicit about specimen acquisition versus culture results, using clinician-confirmed wording without inventing a waiting interval.
Remove "planned nonsurgical treatment" and let the actual neurological, physiological and imaging observations establish eligibility.

reviewRecords.title: Spinal infection: worsening bone imaging during clinical recovery
fairness: Improving pain/function, defervescence and falling CRP must be reconciled with more prominent bony/disc MRI changes. Continuing pathogen-directed treatment is defensible when no new neural compression, collection or deformity is present.
The image is a genuinely conflicting signal rather than decorative detail. Broadening treatment and operative debridement represent credible overinterpretations of radiographic progression.
Necessary negative structural findings preserve a single best answer and should not be removed as mere cue words.
This node stands alone. Its final sentence mentions new mechanical problems as a future boundary, which scaffolds the companion loading question; that downstream effect is assessed separately.
suggestions: Preserve the separation between clinical response, bony imaging evolution and neural/mechanical complications.
Do not convert this answer into an antibiotic stopping rule or a rule that all worsening imaging is harmless; retain needs_clinician_review.

reviewRecords.title: New loading pain and vertebral collapse: next acquisition
clarityIssues: The item does not establish whether standing for an acquisition is safe in this patient with severe loading pain and progressive vertebral collapse, or whether the treating spine team has assessed that question.

cues.phrase: pain now appeared on standing and settled when recumbent
cues.why: Only one choice says "Standing"; both competitors explicitly say "supine".

cues.phrase: alignment had only been assessed lying down
cues.why: This names the unperformed loaded acquisition, effectively supplying the answer.

cues.phrase: New neural or mechanical problems would require a different assessment
cues.why: The preceding node explanation already primes the new mechanical branch, further reducing independent inference.

fairness: A mechanical complication despite improving inflammatory markers is a plausible concern. However, the safety and comparative ranking of standing radiographs versus additional MRI/specialist-directed assessment cannot be confidently settled from this visible record in an offline review.
Unchanged neurology and falling CRP do not themselves establish safe loading. This is an unresolved clinical qualification, not a claim that standing films are always contraindicated.
The sequence is coherent, and the new symptoms stand alone, but the option pattern reduces the scored task to matching position words.
Choosing the precise loaded acquisition in vertebral infection is a narrower specialty objective than recognizing instability and obtaining appropriate spine assessment.
suggestions: Have Melissa confirm acquisition safety and the intended diagnostic pathway for this exact collapse/pain scenario before accepting a key.
Prefer testing the high-yield recognition and next assessment of a mechanical complication, with credible alternatives and a clearly defined care stage.
If imaging acquisition remains the objective, supply actual relevant safety findings without a teaching sentence that simply authorizes standing, and remove the named-omission cue.
Avoid fixed collapse or angulation thresholds unless separately sourced and clinically approved.

reviewRecords.title: Compatible spinal findings with S. aureus bacteremia
clarityIssues: "Which etiologic treatment plan" is unnecessarily abstract; the clinical choice is whether the available microbiology is sufficient to start directed treatment or tissue diagnosis is still needed.

cues.phrase: Begin S. aureus-directed treatment using the blood isolate
cues.why: This is the only option that uses the supplied organism and susceptibility report.

cues.phrase: Defer treatment until image-guided vertebral biopsy returns / Defer treatment until open operative biopsy returns
cues.why: Both distractors repeat the same delay premise, with the open option additionally unsupported by the stated lack of an operative indication.

fairness: Compatible vertebral findings with convincing S. aureus bloodstream evidence can support directed treatment without a separate routine vertebral biopsy. The explanation appropriately limits this principle rather than applying it to every positive culture.
The current task mainly applies that single organism-concordance rule; there is no meaningful remaining competing etiologic interpretation to make two consequential steps.
The first node is self-contained. It establishes the organism for the later complication without revealing decompression.
suggestions: Use a plain next-plan task.
Build a real concordance question in which interpreting the supplied organism/site findings changes whether biopsy adds needed information, without turning this into an unsupported universal rule.
Replace duplicate treatment-deferral alternatives with credible plans at the same decision stage; keep active bacteremia treatment requirements explicit and clinician-reviewed.

reviewRecords.title: Spinal infection: new neurological compression

cues.phrase: An expanding dorsal epidural collection compressed the lumbar neural elements
cues.why: The imaging already states compression, echoed by the only option offering "decompression".

cues.phrase: Urgent spine-surgical assessment for decompression
cues.why: Only this choice addresses the explicitly progressive weakness and bladder dysfunction; the alternatives investigate microbiology or broaden known-active therapy.

fairness: Progressive bilateral weakness and new retention with demonstrated epidural compression support urgent spine-surgical evaluation. No confident clinical error is identified in the explanation.
The falling CRP is a relevant warning against false reassurance but does not make two independent steps when both neurological compromise and its compressive explanation are explicitly supplied.
The case follows directed therapy coherently and independently provides the current MRI, neurological change and treatment response. Earlier feedback does not disclose this answer.
suggestions: Retain the red flags and urgent action; never remove essential safety findings to make this harder.
Either obtain explicit acceptance as an easy high-yield emergency-recognition item or ask a genuinely distinct consequential decision with credible competing urgent plans.
Avoid claiming a difficult two-step item solely because laboratory improvement conflicts with an already stated compressive emergency.

reviewRecords.title: Postoperative foot drop versus pre-existing lumbar imaging
fairness: The motor map, including preserved inversion and hip abduction, must be interpreted against pre-existing foraminal narrowing. Fibular-directed electrodiagnostic localization is the defensible next investigation among these choices before attributing the deficit to the lumbar image.

The old MRI creates a meaningful anchoring competitor; choosing physiology over repeating spine imaging requires applying the examination to the causal question. Tibial-focused assessment is weaker but anatomically in the same differential territory.
A prior MRI abnormality is not excluded as causal merely because it predates symptoms; the explanation appropriately uses the current motor distribution as the stronger discriminator.
The first node is self-contained and does not predict the later focal fullness or structural test.
suggestions: In feedback, make clear that a complete localization study may sample relevant nonfibular muscles; the short option label should not imply fibular conduction alone conclusively excludes radiculopathy.
Retain the clinically important distinction between postoperative temporal association and proof of a positioning/anesthetic cause; retain needs_clinician_review.

reviewRecords.title: Persistent localized foot drop with focal fullness

cues.phrase: fibular head
cues.why: The exhibit repeats this site three times and the only new investigation names that exact site.

cues.phrase: Repeat the same fibular electrodiagnostic protocol / Repeat lumbar MRI with foraminal assessment
cues.why: Both competitors repeat existing investigations; the key is the only new structural inquiry.

cues.phrase: No dressing, splint edge or positioning device remains in contact with the fibular head
cues.why: This preemptively removes the obvious external-compression pathway without a competing action that makes the exclusion consequential.

fairness: Concordant focal physiological localization and palpable fullness support local structural evaluation. Targeted ultrasound is defensible among these options; the case does not prove a particular mass or surgical mechanism.
The localized problem is already interpreted for the learner. Selecting the only new local structural test is a single follow-up decision with weak competitors.
The later result is coherent and self-contained. Earlier feedback has already undermined the lumbar MRI explanation, making that repeated distractor even less competitive in sequence.
suggestions: Compare plausible local structural assessments or management paths at the same stage, with patient-specific observations that justify one ranking.
Remove the same-protocol repeat as a novelty giveaway; do not recycle the already-defeated lumbar anchoring error as the main difficulty.
Retain the high-yield postoperative nerve-injury objective but require structural information to alter a real next decision.

choices.counterfactual: If the prior report already contained an adequate concordant median assessment, repeating it merely because the ulnar study was normal would add little.
