runtimeQuestions.stem: Which study should be obtained to complete {patientName}'s pre-intervention hand evaluation?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Symptoms
items.value: Nighttime tingling affects the thumb, index and middle fingers; placing the wrist in flexion reproduces it.

items.label: Outside study
items.value: The report lists ulnar motor conduction across the elbow and needle sampling of first dorsal interosseous; these were normal.

items.label: Care course
items.value: Symptoms continue despite a neutral wrist splint; a hand surgeon has requested objective localization before an intervention.

answerChoices.label: Median conduction across the wrist
answerChoices.rationale: The symptom map suggests a wrist-level median process, but the outside study evaluated a different nerve and segment. A targeted median study addresses that gap.

answerChoices.label: Ulnar conduction across the elbow
answerChoices.rationale: This repeats the documented normal territory rather than assessing the symptomatic wrist-level median segment.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This repeats the documented normal territory rather than assessing the symptomatic wrist-level median segment.

answerChoices.label: Median conduction across the forearm
answerChoices.rationale: A forearm-segment assessment does not directly test the suspected wrist-level conduction abnormality.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A forearm-segment assessment does not directly test the suspected wrist-level conduction abnormality.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: A normal result applies to the nerve and segment actually examined. The symptom map and the prior study scope together justify median testing at the wrist; a positive history is not itself an order to operate.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which treatment plan should be recommended for {patientName}'s worsening hand deficit?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: New study
items.value: The interpreting physician documents focal median conduction slowing at the wrist with reduced thenar motor response; sampled proximal muscles are preserved.

items.label: Current function
items.value: The thumb cannot lift away from the palm against resistance, and the thenar contour has become visibly flatter.

items.label: Treatment course
items.value: The wrist splint and a prior carpal-tunnel corticosteroid injection gave only temporary relief; numbness and hand clumsiness are worsening.

answerChoices.label: Hand-surgical assessment for carpal tunnel release
answerChoices.rationale: Concordant focal testing, progressive motor loss and failed nonsurgical care support surgical assessment rather than another symptom-only trial.

answerChoices.label: Another carpal-tunnel corticosteroid injection
answerChoices.rationale: A prior temporary sensory response does not address the new progressive motor deficit.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A prior temporary sensory response does not address the new progressive motor deficit.

answerChoices.label: Another trial of neutral wrist splinting
answerChoices.rationale: The current motor and functional deterioration outweighs the rationale for extending the same unsuccessful initial measure.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The current motor and functional deterioration outweighs the rationale for extending the same unsuccessful initial measure.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: Worsening motor function changes the decision after localization. Surgical assessment is appropriate; this item does not choose an operative technique, predict complete recovery or impose a fixed symptom duration.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which electrodiagnostic assessment best resolves the remaining localization question for {patientName}?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Symptoms
items.value: Little/ring-finger tingling accompanies prolonged elbow flexion; finger spreading has become weaker.

items.label: Outside electrodiagnosis
items.value: An averaged ulnar motor velocity across a long elbow segment was reported normal. Needle examination found abnormalities in ulnar intrinsic muscles but not in sampled non-ulnar muscles.

items.label: Examination
items.value: Pressure behind the medial epicondyle reproduces the familiar tingling; neck movement does not change it.

answerChoices.label: Short-segment ulnar studies at the elbow
answerChoices.rationale: A short focal abnormal segment can be diluted by a longer normal segment. More local sampling addresses the discordance.

answerChoices.label: Repeat averaged ulnar studies over the same span
answerChoices.rationale: The same averaging can miss the same short focal segment. The symptom/examination data warrant a more localizing approach.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The same averaging can miss the same short focal segment. The symptom/examination data warrant a more localizing approach.

answerChoices.label: Median studies across the wrist segment
answerChoices.rationale: The clinical and needle findings center on an ulnar process, not a median wrist process.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The clinical and needle findings center on an ulnar process, not a median wrist process.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: Interpret a normal averaged result in the context of the actual acquisition. Short-segment ulnar assessment can reveal a focal elbow lesion. No conduction cutoff or numerical sensitivity claim is required.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which imaging study best addresses {patientName}'s remaining elbow symptoms?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: New testing
items.value: Short-segment studies now localize focal dysfunction at the elbow.

items.label: Residual problem
items.value: Tingling and a palpable snap occur as the elbow moves from extension into flexion; neither occurs with the arm held still.

items.label: Previous imaging
items.value: A stored resting ultrasound shows no mass; it contains no flexion/extension acquisition.

answerChoices.label: Dynamic elbow ultrasound during flexion and extension
answerChoices.rationale: The unresolved issue is movement of the nerve or adjacent structures. A resting image does not test the symptomatic maneuver.

answerChoices.label: Repeat resting elbow ultrasound in extension
answerChoices.rationale: Another static acquisition repeats the condition in which the event does not occur.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Another static acquisition repeats the condition in which the event does not occur.

answerChoices.label: Static elbow MRI with the arm extended
answerChoices.rationale: A static MRI may define masses but does not best reproduce the observed motion-dependent nerve event.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A static MRI may define masses but does not best reproduce the observed motion-dependent nerve event.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: The prior scan answers a resting structural question. Symptoms linked to elbow motion require dynamic assessment; finding nerve movement does not by itself select a specific operation.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which additional electrodiagnostic target is most useful for {patientName}'s current shoulder deficit?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Operation
items.value: An outside posterior-triangle cervical lymph-node excision preceded a new lower resting shoulder and reduced overhead reach.

items.label: Examination
items.value: Resisted shoulder shrug is weak. The medial scapular border does not lift during forward pushing; active glenohumeral abduction is stronger when the scapula is manually supported.

items.label: Outside study
items.value: Needle testing of deltoid and biceps was normal.

answerChoices.label: Needle examination of trapezius
answerChoices.rationale: The neck operation and weak shrug implicate trapezius function. Normal deltoid and biceps do not directly assess that motor territory.

answerChoices.label: Needle examination of serratus anterior
answerChoices.rationale: The dominant deficit is weak shrug and shoulder droop, rather than the forward-push pattern of serratus weakness.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The dominant deficit is weak shrug and shoulder droop, rather than the forward-push pattern of serratus weakness.

answerChoices.label: Repeat needle examination of deltoid
answerChoices.rationale: The prior normal sample did not evaluate the muscle implicated by weak shrug and scapular support response.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The prior normal sample did not evaluate the muscle implicated by weak shrug and scapular support response.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: The negative test is specific to the sampled muscles. A trapezius-directed evaluation addresses this postoperative motor pattern; the findings do not establish transection or prescribe repair.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which additional electrodiagnostic target best addresses {patientName}'s current shoulder deficit?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Operation
items.value: Shoulder fatigue and loss of forward reach began after an outside axillary node procedure.

items.label: Examination
items.value: The medial border lifts away from the chest on forward pushing. Shrug is strong, and passive shoulder elevation remains full.

items.label: Outside study
items.value: The report describes normal trapezius and deltoid needle samples.

answerChoices.label: Needle examination of serratus anterior
answerChoices.rationale: The examination implicates serratus-supported scapular motion. The normal sampled muscles do not test that territory.

answerChoices.label: Repeat needle examination of trapezius
answerChoices.rationale: The preserved shrug and already normal trapezius sampling do not address the untested forward-push deficit.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The preserved shrug and already normal trapezius sampling do not address the untested forward-push deficit.

answerChoices.label: Repeat needle examination of deltoid
answerChoices.rationale: The abnormal scapular motion during pushing points away from repeating a glenohumeral muscle sample.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The abnormal scapular motion during pushing points away from repeating a glenohumeral muscle sample.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: The symptomatic motor territory must be examined. The forward-push findings and preserved shrug support serratus-directed testing rather than another already normal sample; no recovery timeline or operative indication follows from this item.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which initial outside-hospital plan best fit {patientName}'s knee presentation at this stage?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Initial outside examination
items.value: The right native knee was swollen and warm, with a palpable effusion and marked pain throughout passive motion. Fever and an elevated CRP were recorded.

items.label: Systemic assessment
items.value: Blood pressure, mentation and peripheral perfusion remained normal; no organ dysfunction was documented.

items.label: Treatment record
items.value: Blood cultures had been collected. The medication record showed analgesia but no antimicrobial administration.

answerChoices.label: Aspirate the knee, then start empiric antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: The joint findings warrant urgent microbiologic sampling. In this stable recorded stage, sampling before antibiotics avoids unnecessary loss of diagnostic yield.

answerChoices.label: Start empiric antibiotics, then aspirate the knee
answerChoices.rationale: The record supplies a stable opportunity for joint sampling; giving antibiotics first can compromise microbiologic confirmation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The record supplies a stable opportunity for joint sampling; giving antibiotics first can compromise microbiologic confirmation.

answerChoices.label: Obtain knee MRI, then aspirate the knee
answerChoices.rationale: The clinically evident effusion can be sampled without first resolving a structural MRI question. MRI-first postpones the key microbiologic step.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The clinically evident effusion can be sampled without first resolving a structural MRI question. MRI-first postpones the key microbiologic step.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: Concerning native-joint findings require synovial microbiology. The stable systemic observations permit joint sampling before empiric antibiotics. The sequence changes when sepsis makes treatment delay unsafe.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which interim treatment plan best fit {patientName}'s knee while cultures were pending?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Aspirate
items.value: The fluid was cloudy, with numerous neutrophils and monosodium urate crystals. The Gram stain showed no organisms; cultures were still incubating.

items.label: Current course
items.value: The patient remained febrile with severe pain on passive knee motion and persistent effusion after aspiration.

items.label: Treatment
items.value: Empiric intravenous antibiotics had been started after sampling.

answerChoices.label: Continue empiric antimicrobial treatment
answerChoices.rationale: Crystals and a negative Gram stain do not exclude infection. The ongoing inflammatory joint/systemic course sustains concern while microbiology is unresolved.

answerChoices.label: Replace antimicrobials with oral colchicine
answerChoices.rationale: The crystals explain a competing inflammatory process but do not settle whether infection also exists.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The crystals explain a competing inflammatory process but do not settle whether infection also exists.

answerChoices.label: Replace antimicrobials with intra-articular steroid
answerChoices.rationale: Injecting steroid does not address the unresolved infectious possibility in a persistently febrile painful joint.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Injecting steroid does not address the unresolved infectious possibility in a persistently febrile painful joint.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: Interpret crystals and Gram stain within the whole record. Neither finding safely closes the infectious branch here; maintain the empiric plan while cultures and urgent orthopedic reassessment continue.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which additional laboratory test best addresses {patientName}'s unresolved knee findings?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Sampling chronology
items.value: Intravenous antibiotics were administered at the referring hospital before the first knee aspiration.

items.label: Microbiology
items.value: The first fluid culture remained negative after the laboratory completed routine incubation; repeat fluid was again cloudy and neutrophil-rich.

items.label: Current course
items.value: Pain on passive knee motion, effusion and fever persisted during treatment.

answerChoices.label: Bacterial PCR on synovial fluid
answerChoices.rationale: Antibiotic exposure before sampling can limit culture recovery. Synovial molecular testing addresses persistent microbiologic uncertainty.

answerChoices.label: Repeat Gram stain on stored synovial fluid
answerChoices.rationale: Another stain is less useful than adding a molecular method to this already culture-negative antibiotic-exposed workup.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Another stain is less useful than adding a molecular method to this already culture-negative antibiotic-exposed workup.

answerChoices.label: Repeat crystal microscopy on synovial fluid
answerChoices.rationale: Crystals cannot settle the persistent concern for a bacterial process after antibiotic-exposed negative cultures.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Crystals cannot settle the persistent concern for a bacterial process after antibiotic-exposed negative cultures.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: The treatment-before-sampling sequence limits what a negative culture establishes. Synovial PCR can add information in this setting; its result still requires interpretation with the clinical record.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which requested analysis should receive priority for {patientName}'s limited repeat knee aspirate?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: New result
items.value: The synovial bacterial PCR detected S. aureus; the original culture had not produced an isolate.

items.label: Repeat aspiration
items.value: The laboratory received a small amount of newly aspirated fluid and reported that it could not perform every requested test.

items.label: Requested tests
items.value: Bacterial culture, leukocyte count and crystal examination were all requested.

answerChoices.label: Bacterial culture of the new aspirate
answerChoices.rationale: Bacterial identification remains the priority when volume is limited. A PCR detection has not provided a viable isolate for standard susceptibility testing.

answerChoices.label: Leukocyte count of the new aspirate
answerChoices.rationale: A numerical inflammatory count cannot substitute for bacterial identification in this unresolved culture workup.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A numerical inflammatory count cannot substitute for bacterial identification in this unresolved culture workup.

answerChoices.label: Crystal microscopy of the new aspirate
answerChoices.rationale: Crystals could coexist with infection and should not displace bacterial identification when fluid is scarce.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Crystals could coexist with infection and should not displace bacterial identification when fluid is scarce.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: Use scarce synovial material to preserve bacterial identification first. The positive molecular result does not create a cultured isolate, and an inflammatory count or crystal result cannot replace it.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which next treatment step best fit {patientName}'s knee at this recorded reassessment?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Earlier care
items.value: The hospital performed an arthroscopic washout of an infected native knee and started antibiotics active against the recovered organism.

items.label: Interval findings
items.value: Purulent drainage and a reaccumulating effusion continued; passive motion became more painful, and CRP rose on serial measurements.

items.label: Treatment verification
items.value: The susceptibility report and medication record remained concordant, with no missed antimicrobial doses.

answerChoices.label: Repeat arthroscopic knee debridement
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent purulence, deteriorating function and rising inflammatory markers support failed source control despite an active antimicrobial regimen.

answerChoices.label: Change to broader intravenous antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: The available susceptibility and administration record do not identify inadequate antimicrobial activity; the local purulent course requires renewed source-control attention.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The available susceptibility and administration record do not identify inadequate antimicrobial activity; the local purulent course requires renewed source-control attention.

answerChoices.label: Continue the current intravenous antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: Passive continuation overlooks combined evidence of local treatment failure.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Passive continuation overlooks combined evidence of local treatment failure.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: An active antibiotic does not establish adequate source control. The combined local deterioration and inflammatory trend support repeat orthopedic debridement assessment, without claiming that any single CRP value mandates surgery.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which evaluation plan best fit {patientName}'s evolving leg deficit at that outside-hospital stage?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: New postoperative course
items.value: After the repeat knee procedure, lateral-leg tingling appeared. The anesthesia record documented return of strength and sensation after the block before this complaint.

items.label: Serial examination
items.value: Ankle dorsiflexion and eversion were initially present but became progressively weaker on repeated examinations. Distal perfusion remained intact.

items.label: Early study
items.value: Electrodiagnostic testing obtained near symptom onset was reported normal; the motor deterioration continued afterward.

answerChoices.label: Urgent neurology or peripheral-nerve consultation
answerChoices.rationale: Progressive objective motor loss requires urgent assessment despite an early normal study. A fixed interval before repeat EDX must not become a reason to defer clinical evaluation.

answerChoices.label: Scheduled repeat electrodiagnosis with later clinic review
answerChoices.rationale: A later EDX may become useful, but its timing does not resolve the need to assess current progression.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A later EDX may become useful, but its timing does not resolve the need to assess current progression.

answerChoices.label: Supervised rehabilitation with routine clinic review
answerChoices.rationale: Routine recovery management does not address new progressive motor loss after the block resolved.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Routine recovery management does not address new progressive motor loss after the block resolved.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: Current objective progression takes precedence over an early normal test. Seek urgent neurologic/peripheral-nerve assessment; postoperative timing does not establish which operative, anesthetic or compressive mechanism caused the deficit.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which next spine study best fit {patientName}'s initial outside evaluation?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Symptoms
items.value: Focal lumbar pain persisted at rest and repeatedly woke the patient from sleep.

items.label: Outside evaluation
items.value: The patient was afebrile, with unchanged leg strength and sensation. CRP remained above the laboratory reference range.

items.label: Existing imaging
items.value: Lumbar radiographs showed osteophytes and disc-space narrowing without an acute fracture; no cross-sectional spine imaging had been performed.

answerChoices.label: Contrast-enhanced lumbar spine MRI
answerChoices.rationale: The infection history and inflammatory course remain concerning despite absent fever and degenerative radiographs. MRI evaluates early vertebral/disc and adjacent soft-tissue infection.

answerChoices.label: Noncontrast lumbar spine CT
answerChoices.rationale: CT is useful for bony detail but is not the preferred next assessment of this suspected disc/soft-tissue process when MRI is feasible.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: CT is useful for bony detail but is not the preferred next assessment of this suspected disc/soft-tissue process when MRI is feasible.

answerChoices.label: Technetium lumbar bone scan
answerChoices.rationale: A bone scan is not preferred when MRI can assess the vertebral and adjacent soft-tissue process.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A bone scan is not preferred when MRI can assess the vertebral and adjacent soft-tissue process.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: Afebrile status and degenerative films do not adequately explain persistent focal pain with continuing inflammatory evidence. MRI addresses the vertebral/disc and adjacent soft-tissue question.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which diagnostic-treatment sequence best fit {patientName}'s spinal findings at this stage?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: New imaging
items.value: MRI showed opposing endplate marrow abnormalities, intervening disc enhancement and adjacent paraspinal inflammation; there was no neural compression or drainable epidural collection.

items.label: Microbiology
items.value: Blood cultures collected before antibiotics remained negative after routine incubation.

items.label: Current examination
items.value: The patient remained normotensive, alert and neurologically unchanged; spine specialists planned nonsurgical treatment.

answerChoices.label: Obtain image-guided disc/endplate samples, then select antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: Stable nonsurgical disease without an identified organism permits targeted microbiology/histology before empiric therapy reduces yield.

answerChoices.label: Start empiric antibiotics, then obtain disc/endplate samples
answerChoices.rationale: Stable physiology and negative blood cultures leave a pre-treatment tissue-diagnosis opportunity.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Stable physiology and negative blood cultures leave a pre-treatment tissue-diagnosis opportunity.

answerChoices.label: Obtain open operative disc/endplate samples, then select antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: No operative indication or failed image-guided sampling makes open sampling the preferred initial route.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: No operative indication or failed image-guided sampling makes open sampling the preferred initial route.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: Organism evidence and current stability determine the sampling sequence. Stable culture-negative nonsurgical disease supports image-guided sampling before empiric treatment; deterioration changes the priority.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which treatment response plan best fits {patientName}'s current spinal record?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Established disease
items.value: The outside team treated culture-confirmed vertebral infection with susceptibility-concordant antibiotics.

items.label: Clinical course
items.value: The patient was afebrile; pain and walking tolerance improved. Leg strength and bladder/bowel function were unchanged. CRP fell toward the reference range.

items.label: Repeat MRI
items.value: The report described more prominent endplate/disc abnormalities but no new epidural collection, neural compression or deformity.

answerChoices.label: Continue the planned pathogen-directed treatment
answerChoices.rationale: Clinical/inflammatory improvement can coexist with evolving bony MRI abnormalities; the scan does not establish failure here.

answerChoices.label: Replace treatment with broader empiric antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: The scan does not establish resistance or inadequate treatment during documented clinical response.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The scan does not establish resistance or inadequate treatment during documented clinical response.

answerChoices.label: Proceed to operative spinal debridement
answerChoices.rationale: No compression, deformity or clinical failure is documented to supply a surgical indication.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: No compression, deformity or clinical failure is documented to supply a surgical indication.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: The response supports continuing planned treatment. MRI normalization need not coincide with clinical improvement. New neural or mechanical problems would require a different assessment; no treatment-stop rule is asserted.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which next imaging acquisition best addresses {patientName}'s new symptom pattern?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Later course
items.value: Fever remained absent and CRP continued to fall, but severe focal back pain now appeared on standing and settled when recumbent.

items.label: Examination
items.value: Leg strength, sensation and bladder/bowel function remained unchanged.

items.label: Available imaging
items.value: A supine CT showed further collapse at the previously infected segment; alignment had only been assessed lying down.

answerChoices.label: Standing spinal radiographs compared with supine imaging
answerChoices.rationale: The new loading pain and collapse raise an alignment question that unloaded images may not resolve.

answerChoices.label: Repeat supine spinal CT with the same positioning
answerChoices.rationale: Another unloaded acquisition does not best test whether alignment changes under load.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Another unloaded acquisition does not best test whether alignment changes under load.

answerChoices.label: Contrast spinal MRI with the patient supine
answerChoices.rationale: MRI evaluates infection/neural structures; the new uncertainty concerns loading with unchanged neurology and improving inflammation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: MRI evaluates infection/neural structures; the new uncertainty concerns loading with unchanged neurology and improving inflammation.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: Infection response and mechanical competence differ. Loading pain with collapse warrants assessment of alignment under load; no angle, height-loss or operation threshold is invented.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which etiologic treatment plan best fit {patientName}'s concordant spinal and blood findings?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Blood cultures
items.value: Separate blood-culture sets obtained before antibiotics grew methicillin-susceptible S. aureus, with a complete susceptibility report.

items.label: Spinal findings
items.value: MRI showed contiguous disc/endplate inflammatory abnormalities and adjacent soft-tissue inflammation at the site of focal back pain.

items.label: Clinical stage
items.value: The patient was stable without neural compression or a current operative indication.

answerChoices.label: Begin S. aureus-directed treatment using the blood isolate
answerChoices.rationale: Typical-organism bacteremia and compatible spinal imaging provide a concordant etiologic basis; a separate diagnostic vertebral biopsy is not routinely required in this exact setting.

answerChoices.label: Defer treatment until image-guided vertebral biopsy returns
answerChoices.rationale: This delays directed care to repeat an etiologic determination already supported by concordant typical-organism evidence.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This delays directed care to repeat an etiologic determination already supported by concordant typical-organism evidence.

answerChoices.label: Defer treatment until open operative biopsy returns
answerChoices.rationale: There is neither unresolved etiologic evidence nor a separate surgical indication favoring open diagnostic acquisition.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: There is neither unresolved etiologic evidence nor a separate surgical indication favoring open diagnostic acquisition.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: This is a narrow concordance rule for S. aureus bloodstream infection with compatible spinal findings. It does not apply to every positive bottle or discordant lesion and does not define a drug regimen or duration.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which next treatment plan best fit {patientName}'s new spinal findings at that recorded stage?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Treatment response
items.value: Directed antibiotics reduced fever and CRP. The susceptibility report remained concordant.

items.label: New examination
items.value: Progressive bilateral leg weakness and new inability to empty the bladder appeared after previously normal walking and voiding.

items.label: New MRI
items.value: An expanding dorsal epidural collection compressed the lumbar neural elements at the affected segment.

answerChoices.label: Urgent spine-surgical assessment for decompression
answerChoices.rationale: New motor/bladder dysfunction with compression establishes an urgent neural problem despite biochemical improvement.

answerChoices.label: Broaden antimicrobial therapy with medical reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: Antimicrobial activity does not relieve demonstrated neural compression or replace urgent surgical evaluation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Antimicrobial activity does not relieve demonstrated neural compression or replace urgent surgical evaluation.

answerChoices.label: Repeat image-guided vertebral sampling for microbiology
answerChoices.rationale: The organism is established; the new neural compromise takes priority over repeating an etiologic sample.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The organism is established; the new neural compromise takes priority over repeating an etiologic sample.

runtimeQuestions.explanation: Assess neural function separately from systemic inflammatory response. Progressive motor/bladder dysfunction with epidural compression requires urgent spine-surgical evaluation; no exact decompression deadline or recovery guarantee is asserted.

runtimeQuestions.stem: Which study best clarifies {patientName}'s foot-drop localization before a lumbar intervention is considered?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Outside context
items.value: Right foot drop appeared after a prolonged nonorthopedic operation. A preoperative lumbar MRI already showed right foraminal narrowing.

items.label: Current examination
items.value: Dorsiflexion and eversion are weak; inversion and hip abduction remain strong. Sensory loss affects the dorsal foot.

items.label: Clinical course

answerChoices.rationale: The infection history and inflammatory course remain concerning despite absent fever and degenerative radiographs. MRI evaluates early vertebral/disc and adjacent soft-tissue infection.

answerChoices.label: Noncontrast lumbar spine CT
answerChoices.rationale: CT is useful for bony detail but is not the preferred next assessment of this suspected disc/soft-tissue process when MRI is feasible.

answerChoices.label: Technetium lumbar bone scan
answerChoices.rationale: A bone scan is not preferred when MRI can assess the vertebral and adjacent soft-tissue process.

decisionNodes.explanation: Afebrile status and degenerative films do not adequately explain persistent focal pain with continuing inflammatory evidence. MRI addresses the vertebral/disc and adjacent soft-tissue question.

decisionNodes.stem: Which diagnostic-treatment sequence best fit {patientName}'s spinal findings at this stage?

answerChoices.label: Obtain image-guided disc/endplate samples, then select antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: Stable nonsurgical disease without an identified organism permits targeted microbiology/histology before empiric therapy reduces yield.

answerChoices.label: Start empiric antibiotics, then obtain disc/endplate samples

answerChoices.label: Obtain open operative disc/endplate samples, then select antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: No operative indication or failed image-guided sampling makes open sampling the preferred initial route.

answerChoices.label: Continue the planned pathogen-directed treatment
answerChoices.rationale: Clinical/inflammatory improvement can coexist with evolving bony MRI abnormalities; the scan does not establish failure here.

answerChoices.label: Replace treatment with broader empiric antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: The scan does not establish resistance or inadequate treatment during documented clinical response.

answerChoices.label: Proceed to operative spinal debridement
answerChoices.rationale: No compression, deformity or clinical failure is documented to supply a surgical indication.

decisionNodes.explanation: The response supports continuing planned treatment. MRI normalization need not coincide with clinical improvement. New neural or mechanical problems would require a different assessment; no treatment-stop rule is asserted.

decisionNodes.stem: Which etiologic treatment plan best fit {patientName}'s concordant spinal and blood findings?

answerChoices.label: Begin S. aureus-directed treatment using the blood isolate
answerChoices.rationale: Typical-organism bacteremia and compatible spinal imaging provide a concordant etiologic basis; a separate diagnostic vertebral biopsy is not routinely required in this exact setting.

answerChoices.label: Defer treatment until image-guided vertebral biopsy returns
answerChoices.rationale: This delays directed care to repeat an etiologic determination already supported by concordant typical-organism evidence.

answerChoices.label: Defer treatment until open operative biopsy returns
answerChoices.rationale: There is neither unresolved etiologic evidence nor a separate surgical indication favoring open diagnostic acquisition.

decisionNodes.explanation: This is a narrow concordance rule for S. aureus bloodstream infection with compatible spinal findings. It does not apply to every positive bottle or discordant lesion and does not define a drug regimen or duration.

answerChoices.label: Urgent spine-surgical assessment for decompression
answerChoices.rationale: New motor/bladder dysfunction with compression establishes an urgent neural problem despite biochemical improvement.

answerChoices.label: Broaden antimicrobial therapy with medical reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: Antimicrobial activity does not relieve demonstrated neural compression or replace urgent surgical evaluation.

answerChoices.label: Repeat image-guided vertebral sampling for microbiology
answerChoices.rationale: The organism is established; the new neural compromise takes priority over repeating an etiologic sample.

decisionNodes.explanation: Assess neural function separately from systemic inflammatory response. Progressive motor/bladder dysfunction with epidural compression requires urgent spine-surgical evaluation; no exact decompression deadline or recovery guarantee is asserted.

decisionNodes.stem: Which study best clarifies {patientName}'s foot-drop localization before a lumbar intervention is considered?

answerChoices.label: Fibular nerve conduction and needle EMG
answerChoices.rationale: The motor map favors a fibular-territory process over one affecting additional root muscles. EDX can localize the current deficit rather than assume an older MRI finding caused it.

answerChoices.label: Repeat lumbar MRI with foraminal assessment
answerChoices.rationale: The pre-deficit narrowing does not establish the cause of this nerve-territory pattern. Localization is needed before a lumbar intervention.

answerChoices.label: Tibial nerve conduction and needle EMG
answerChoices.rationale: An isolated tibial-focused assessment does not interrogate the main weak dorsiflexion/eversion territory.

decisionNodes.explanation: Fit the current motor map before assigning causation to an image. Preserved nonfibular functions and an MRI predating the deficit favor fibular-directed EDX. Postoperative timing alone does not prove an anesthetic or positioning cause.

items.label: Current examination
items.value: Dorsiflexion and eversion are weak; inversion and hip abduction remain strong. Sensory loss affects the dorsal foot.

items.label: Clinical course
items.value: The deficit persists; the MRI predates it and no electrodiagnostic localization is available.

decisionNodes.stem: Which next study best addresses the cause of {patientName}'s persistent localized deficit?

answerChoices.label: Targeted nerve ultrasound at the fibular head
answerChoices.rationale: Focal EDX and matching fullness leave a structural cause unresolved. Ultrasound assesses the nerve and adjacent structures there.

answerChoices.label: Repeat the same fibular electrodiagnostic protocol
answerChoices.rationale: Location is established; repeating the protocol does not best characterize the palpable adjacent structure.

answerChoices.label: Repeat lumbar MRI with foraminal assessment
answerChoices.rationale: This does not investigate the concordant peripheral EDX site and local fullness.

decisionNodes.explanation: Focal physiological localization does not establish structural cause. Matching local fullness without ongoing external pressure warrants anatomical assessment; no specific mass type, operative cause or operation is presumed.

claims.statement: Wrist-level median compression can produce nocturnal thumb, index and middle-finger symptoms.
claims.limitation: Pattern supports localization but is not diagnostic from symptoms alone.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: Median nerve conduction testing across the wrist can assess suspected focal wrist-level compression.
claims.limitation: Single occupational guideline supports the targeted test scope; no mandate for routine EDX in every typical CTS presentation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: Thenar weakness or wasting can indicate more advanced median nerve injury in carpal tunnel syndrome.
claims.limitation: Motor findings must fit the full examination; no numerical severity boundary is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: Severe or worsening carpal tunnel symptoms after unsuccessful nonsurgical care warrant surgical-specialist assessment.
claims.limitation: Referral does not mandate surgery, select an operative technique or promise recovery.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: Elbow-level ulnar compression can cause little/ring-finger symptoms and intrinsic hand weakness.
claims.limitation: Single open review; symptoms require localization rather than labeling all ulnar complaints cubital tunnel.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: Short-segment ulnar conduction assessment can identify focal elbow disease missed by a longer averaged segment.
claims.limitation: Single narrative review; qualitative protocol scope only, not sensitivity, segment-length or velocity cutoffs.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: Dynamic ultrasound can assess ulnar nerve movement at the elbow when symptoms occur during flexion.
claims.limitation: Single open review; movement must correlate with symptoms and does not automatically mandate transposition.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: Progressive or complete postoperative neural deficits warrant urgent specialist evaluation.
claims.limitation: Older society advisory; no exact interval or claim that anesthesia necessarily caused the injury. Full 2015 update was inaccessible.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: Neurophysiologic testing can help establish the location and extent of a postoperative peripheral nerve deficit.
claims.limitation: Older society advisory; a normal study outside the symptomatic motor territory is not a direct test of that territory.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: An early normal neurophysiologic study does not reliably exclude all evolving peripheral nerve injury.
claims.limitation: Older society advisory; no fixed waiting period or universal early-test sensitivity asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: The spinal accessory nerve supplies trapezius, whose weakness can produce shoulder droop and impaired shrug.
claims.limitation: Single open narrative review for stable anatomy; not evidence that a surgical wound transected the nerve.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: The long thoracic nerve supplies serratus anterior, whose weakness can produce medial scapular winging on forward pushing.
claims.limitation: Single open narrative review; no recovery probability, image interpretation or operative timing rule.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the exact constructed clinic or outside-hospital chart-review context.

claims.statement: Suspected native-joint infection should be evaluated with prompt synovial aspiration and microbiologic analysis.
claims.limitation: Clinical signs and crystals cannot replace microbiology; no single cell-count threshold is used.
